title: The free uniform spanning forest is a factor of IID

issues.location: Section 5 (Measurability on varying graphs) / Prop. 2.3 eq. (canonical-finite-formula)
issues.description: The paper only sketches why the rule is Borel on graph space. The inner limit in m of the finite weighted-tree ratios is used as if it were a Borel function of (G,U,e), but on graph space it should be written as a limsup or lim inf (it exists for every graph, so this is easy to fix). Re-rooting at other edges inside the Picard iteration is also only sketched.
issues.evidence: 'every b_{e,S_n(e)}(t,y) is the limit of a finite weighted-tree ratio on H_m(e) as m→∞ ... This exact order of limits makes the formula Borel' — no explicit argument that the pointwise limit is Borel on the space of labeled rooted graphs.

coverage: Read all six section files in full: introduction, response, observation, decoder, implementation and strongly-rayleigh. Checked each step of the main chain: (1) the weighted-tree response, using covariance = -c_e c_f (a_e^T L^{-1} a_f)^2 and a fixed tree size to get the row sum 2p(1-p); (2) the free-limit construction via the cycle-space projection; (3) finite tilts of the FUSF as limits of tilted spanning-tree laws, which carry the 1/2 Lipschitz bound; (4) the sup-norm Lipschitz property of the limsup drift; (5) the posterior identity (Girsanov endpoint likelihood plus martingale convergence) and the innovation lemma (conditional characteristic functions, O(h^{3/2}) error per step); (6) Picard existence and uniqueness for every continuous input, the pathwise identity Y=Z(Ŵ), and readout at integer times; (7) the edge-noise allocation from vertex labels and its equivariance; (8) the strongly Rayleigh row bound via symmetric homogenization (BBL Thm 4.2) and the Rayleigh inequality, and the equivariance from translated exhaustions hF_n. Python checks: the tree covariance-row identity holds to 1e-15 on K5 with random weights, and the SR bound sum_j |Cov| ≤ 2p(1-p) holds for tilted random determinantal processes.
main_claim: One Borel, root-independent, equivariant rule produces the FUSF from IID vertex labels on every infinite, connected, locally finite, simple graph. Every translation-invariant strongly Rayleigh law on a countable group (including invariant determinantal processes) is a factor of IID. The method is stochastic localization: a uniform sup-norm response bound of 1/2 makes the drift equation uniquely solvable for every input, so a deterministic inverse exists.
sibling_notes: The family 231 board was empty when I checked. The abstract sampling criterion (Prop. 4.2: uniformly Lipschitz finite tilts imply FIID) may be reused by companion papers; it looked sound to me.
